sectionTwo.heading: A Legacy That Began With One Truck
paragraphs: Our legacy traces back to 1954 and the vision of Mr. Abdul Rahim, who started with a single truck and went on to establish Taj Transport Company. That modest beginning grew into Mehran Tankers, a name synonymous with reliability in Pakistan’s transport industry.

Building on this foundation, Mr. Abdul Wahab established Logistics Management International (LMI) in July 2005, structuring the company around fresh thinking, innovative ideas and modern logistics techniques.

milestones.description: Taj Transport Company starts with one truck and grows into Mehran Tankers.
Cartage contractor to Pakistan State Oil (PSO).
Cartage and bridging licensee for Caltex Oil (Pakistan).
Certified as Shell Pakistan general cartage contractor.
Logistics Management International (LMI) is established in July.
Nationwide third-party logistics, built on assured fleet availability.

sectionThree.heading: Care Begins Before the Carrier Moves
paragraphs: Moving vehicles is about more than getting them from A to B. The number of vehicles, their type, the pickup location and the receiving site all affect how a carrier should be configured and loaded, so we plan these details before the vehicle arrives.

Vehicles are positioned and secured according to the carrier’s configuration, then unloaded in a controlled manner at the destination. An assured fleet network of verified trucks and drivers is ready exactly when required, which keeps dealer, fleet and corporate schedules on time.
Our drivers follow our HSE protocols, including pre-trip inspection of the carrier before every dispatch.

items.question: What counts as dry cargo?
items.answer: Non-liquid cargo such as packaged, palletized, bagged and cartoned goods, raw materials and finished products.

items.question: Is my cargo protected during transport?
items.answer: We plan loading and securing around the cargo, and use enclosed or covered vehicles where the cargo needs protection.

items.question: Can you handle recurring dry cargo runs?

items.question: What is the difference between FTL and other road freight?
items.answer: With FTL the whole vehicle is dedicated to your shipment. Other road freight services cover smaller, mixed or specialised movements.

items.question: Can you arrange FTL on a recurring basis?
items.answer: Yes. We plan regular full-load movements around your schedule, with a vehicle ready exactly when required.

items.question: What cargo can go FTL?

items.question: What counts as heavy or project cargo?
items.answer: Oversized or heavy loads, and cargo moved around a specific project schedule and site, such as machinery and industrial components.

items.question: How is it different from flatbed?
items.answer: Flatbed is an equipment type for open-deck cargo. Heavy and project cargo adds route, site and schedule planning around the whole movement.

items.question: Do you serve remote project sites?
items.answer: Yes. Our drivers are trained for highways, link roads, mountain passes and difficult terrain.
